# Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes: Summary
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes is Germany’s largest and oldest private scholarship foundation. Founded in 1925 in Dresden, it was dissolved in 1934 during the National Socialist period and revived in 1948 in Cologne. It provides scholarships to exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates in German universities, EU countries, and Switzerland, regardless of citizenship or age. Selection occurs through nomination by schools, professors, examination boards, competition winners, alums, self-nomination via assessment tests, and nominations for musicians and artists. Admission emphasizes academic excellence, initiative, and social responsibility. In 2023, around 14,888 scholars (including 1,262 doctoral students) were funded, representing about 0.48% of German university students.
Studienstiftung scholarships offer both financial (up to €855 monthly for students, €1,550 for PhDs, plus child support and travel funding) and substantial academic support (summer schools, academies, mentoring, workshops). Regular and special internal/external programs exist, such as research internships and partnerships with institutions like KAUST. In 2023, 71.5% of recipients received a study expense allowance, with women comprising 55.4% of scholars. Its alumni include Nobel laureates, leading scientists, business and political leaders, artists, and journalists, underscoring its prominence in cultivating top German talent.
